title: Aureum Vellus: Guldin Schatz und Kunstkammer with Splendor Solis illustrations (Cod. Sang. 1727)
shelf_note: A German alchemical recipe manuscript (process for raising silver to the Rhenish standard), in keeping with the Aureum Vellus / Trismosin title. No tradition or collection is set, so only the title can be checked; the page matches it.
structure_note: Record 200 carries the handwritten page number 196. A steady offset of 4 suggests unnumbered front leaves, not a misalignment. The 59 backsteps and 62 repeats across 432 numbered pages fit an inconsistently paginated manuscript, or numerals misread from a cursive hand, better than a broken sequence, though this one page cannot settle it. The counts disagree with each other: structure.pages_translated is 0 but pages_translated_field is 517.

pages.layout: single column of cursive German inside a ruled frame; a three-line heading under a smaller repeated title line; page number at top left; catchword "das" at bottom right

ocr_errors.image: Process Eines geheimen gradier ▽ (downward triangle, the water sign: 'Gradier-Wasser', a grading water)
ocr_errors.problem: In both title lines the water sign is read as fire (🜂), so the process is named as the wrong substance

ocr_errors.image: Jn ▽ man darin Baad dz ☉ (water sign again)
ocr_errors.problem: Water is read as mercury, so the medium of the opening operation is changed

ocr_errors.image: ℞ "3" lot ☉, das Laminier dün, Machs mit "3" ℥ (the scribe puts numerals in quotation marks, as in "2", "30")
ocr_errors.problem: The quantity of gold, 3 lot, becomes 'Halbe' (half), so the recipe's dose is lost. 'Machs' is also read as 'die Maß'
'Leuthen' read as 'Leuffen', which the translation turns into 'vagabonds'
'Stuckh' (the procedure or piece) appears to be read as 'Stuhls' (chair), which gives the nonsense 'of the chair'

ocr_errors.image: auf "2" ⊠ (a square with a cross: a time or vessel sign, not the salt sign)
ocr_errors.problem: The duration or unit sign is replaced by 🜔, so the length of the maceration cannot be recovered

ocr_errors.image: thue solches in ein 6, ℞ (the same vessel sign as after 'Kolben' a few lines up)
ocr_errors.problem: A vessel sign is read as silver, so the text says to put the precipitate 'into a Silver'

ocr_errors.image: deß Vogündlenz "2" Lot (hand hard to read here)
ocr_errors.problem: The quantity may be misread ("2" vs 7½), and the substance's name is uncertain

tr_errors.problem: The OCR's misread is carried into the title: the image has a grading WATER (▽). The reader is told the wrong reagent is the subject of the process

tr_errors.english: In **Mercury [☿]**, as in a bath, the **Gold [☉]**
tr_errors.problem: The image says water (▽), not mercury
The image gives 3 lot of gold. The English gives 'half', so the dose is wrong

tr_errors.english: above all not to loose, arrogant vagabonds
tr_errors.problem: Built on the misread 'Leuffen'. The image has 'Leüthen' (people). The added 'above all' is not in the source either
'of the chair' is meaningless here and rests on the misread 'Stuhls'
Nonsensical vessel inherited from the OCR misread
The image reads '"3" ten mall' (the third time), not a third day

other.note: The summary repeats the misreads ('a grading fire', 'using mercury, salts'), so the derived metadata is wrong too

items.quote: original: "Verlutiers"; seal it with luting clay

missing.english: **Silver [☾]** is graded up to the Rhenish standard
missing.why: A general reader will not know that the 'Rhenish standard' is the fineness of Rhenish gold coin, so the aim of the process, to make silver pass as gold of that grade, is lost
'lot' is an old weight (about half an ounce), and the reader needs it to follow the quantities
A cover name for a reagent, left with no word on what kind of substance it is or that it is a code name
An unexplained Arabic-Latin term. The reader cannot tell that it is a cover name the text decodes with the following sign
Cementation vessel: a technical term that a general reader may take literally

book_verdict: The transcription of this cursive alchemical manuscript is mostly sound, but it misreads key signs and a quantity: water becomes fire in the title and mercury in the first line, and '3 lot' of gold becomes 'half'. The fluent English carries all of them, so a reader gets the wrong reagent and the wrong dose.
